Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity: autoscaling & integration follow-up

Samuel 	6 appreciate the clear list. Below are concrete answers and recommended starting configs ahead of the workshop. High-level first, then config snippets.

High-level:
- Autoscaling model: Dedicated uses a combination of reserved pool + burst capacity. The controller scales by adding/removing worker pods using queue length and token-per-second consumption as signals. There is also the option to pin a minimum number of GPUs for strict SLOs.
- Throughput sizing: For transformer-based generation models, estimate throughput in tokens/sec per GPU by model size and batch sizing. Example: gpt-medium-ish (8B) ~ 1.2k-1.5k tokens/sec on an A100-40GB with batching; LLM-llarge (30B) ~ 200-400 tokens/sec. We'll provide per-model numbers in the pre-read.
- Concurrency limits & queues: We recommend a hybrid queue per-model-shard where synchronous requests hit a front-door ingress queue with a configurable concurrency cap (default 64 requests per worker). If concurrency limit is hit, requests are enqueued (FIFO) with a max queue length and an optional low-latency drop policy for non-critical requests.
- Burst behavior: Burst capacity adds extra workers up to a configured max pool size; bursts are gated by a rate-limit token bucket to avoid provisioning thrash.

Integration details (SDK/Auth/Routing):
- SDK setup: Use our Node/Python SDK. Example initialization includes region, api_key, and optional mTLS cert for private deployments.
- Auth: Dedicated supports API key auth for server-to-server, SAML/OIDC for human user flows, and mutual TLS for private networks. We can also enable customer-managed KMS for keys.
- Routing: Policy-based routing is supported (latency-first, cost-first, region-first). You can tag routes for specific models or fallbacks (e.g., use quantized model in low-cost tier).

Structured output & tool calling:
- We validate structured JSON output via a schema enforcement layer in the runtime; tool-calls (function calls) are supported with deterministic fallback if the tool times out.

Embeddings & re-ranker flow:
- Recommended pattern: Run embeddings on Dedicated (GPU-backed) and store vectors in your vector DB. Re-ranking can be a lightweight model (lower cost) or an on-GPU reranker depending on latency/quality needs. We recommend batching embedding writes and reserving a small dedicated pool for reranker to ensure steady latency.

Sample config (high-level):
- min_pool_size: 2 GPUs
- max_pool_size: 10 GPUs
- scale_up_threshold: queue_length > 20 OR token_rate > 70%
- scale_down_threshold: idle_time > 120s
- concurrency_per_worker: 64
- max_queue_length: 500
- burst_token_bucket_rate: 200 requests/min

We'll attach the dedicated_arch_diagram.pdf and a per-model throughput table prior to the workshop. If you can share expected QPS distribution (peak vs baseline + average request token length) we can tune these numbers to more precise values.

Sam 	6 thanks, and great questions. Quick answers and confirmed next steps: 

- Burst billing: burst GPUs are billed at the same unit rate as reserved GPUs and charged by the minute with a 1-minute granularity; there is also a short warm-up provisioning window (~30	690s) depending on model size. We'll have exact billing granularity in the quote.
- Concurrency isolation: concurrency caps are applied per-worker instance. You can pin a model to its own worker pool for strict isolation; otherwise multiple models on a worker share the concurrency budget. We'll include a sample pinning policy.
- Safe fallback: recommended approach is a warm fallback pool (quantized model variant) in the same region with a shorter request timeout and early-failover policy to avoid tail amplification.
